summary: U.S. markets opened mixed on Monday, August 17, with tech resilience offsetting broader weakness as the S&P 500 fell 0.28% while the Nasdaq Composite edged up 0.21% on AI optimism. Chipmakers rallied after Anthropic's revenue surge bolstered confidence in sustained AI capital expenditure, though Middle East tensions and rising oil prices near $89 kept investors cautious. The White House is set to host a major crypto meeting Wednesday with SEC Chair Paul Atkins, CFTC leadership, and executives from Coinbase, Ripple, and Gemini, though the Senate has pushed the Clarity Act beyond August recess. The NAHB Housing Market Index beat expectations at 35, up from 34, but Treasury yields remain elevated with the 30-year touching highs last seen in 2007. Retail earnings from Home Depot, Walmart, Target, and Lowe's later this week will test consumer resilience, while investors await FOMC minutes Wednesday and Fed Chair Warsh's upcoming Jackson Hole appearance.

signals.title: Anthropic revenue surge fuels AI infrastructure rally
signals.desc: Chipmakers rallied as Anthropic's strong revenue growth reinforces the case for sustained AI datacenter capex and hyperscaler demand.

signals.title: White House crypto meeting set for Wednesday amid regulatory uncertainty
signals.desc: White House meeting with SEC, CFTC, and crypto firms signals engagement, but Clarity Act delay and postponed SEC digital-asset rules maintain policy overhang.

signals.title: Middle East escalation drives oil to $89, Treasury yields spike
signals.desc: Fresh violence in the Middle East pushed Brent crude toward $89 and Treasury 30-year yields to 2007 highs, raising inflationary pressures and rate-hike risks.

signals.title: Housing sentiment beats but remains deeply depressed
signals.desc: NAHB index rose to 35 from 34, beating consensus, but remains below 40 for 16 consecutive months as high rates and construction costs weigh on builders.

signals.title: Workday downgraded by Deutsche Bank and BTIG after 76% rally
signals.desc: Deutsche Bank cut Workday to Hold and BTIG to Neutral after a 76% rebound from June lows, citing valuation concerns post-Silver Lake acquisition chatter.

verdict: Tech resilience battles macro headwinds as AI optimism offsets geopolitical risks and elevated yields, with retail earnings and FOMC minutes poised to set the tone for the week.
